chat.title: Real-time Chat System for ERP
chat.context: Gia Cat Technology Solutions · internal product · sole developer
chat.description: A real-time chat layer built into the ERP platform, covering four kinds of conversation: one-to-one, group, threads attached to a specific ERP document, and channels that inherit the permission groups already defined in the ERP. The last two are the part an off-the-shelf messenger cannot do — a conversation that lives on a purchase order, and access that follows the permission data the system already holds.
responsibilities: Architected and built the full stack: Node.js backend, SSE-based message push, and the PL/SQL data layer
Wrote the browser chat client by hand in JavaScript, consuming the SSE event stream and rendering incoming messages without page reloads
Integrated Oracle CQN with a multi-database registry to detect row-level changes and fan out notifications
Designed the APEX to Node integration path through PL/SQL AJAX callbacks and UTL_HTTP with token-based authentication, keeping the internal server off the public network
Owned production deployment and operations with PM2 and custom start / stop shell scripts
Built CLI verification scripts covering the REST endpoints, CQN callbacks, SSE streams and the connection registry
metrics: ~1 month from zero to production, as sole developer

heartRisk.title: Heart Risk Estimator
heartRisk.description: A heart-disease risk screening tool. The Django API is built so validation is the only route to the model, and the React client renders itself from a schema the server sends — no field name, range or option is hard-coded in the browser.
responsibilities: Trained an AdaBoost ensemble of decision stumps on the UCI Heart Disease dataset, measured it against a single-stump baseline, and exported the fitted model with joblib
Built the Django API so the view binds the JSON body to a form and passes nothing but cleaned data to the classifier
Served the form definition from a schema endpoint and rendered the React client from it
Wrote the interface in React and TypeScript, covered by 15 front-end tests across rendering, submission, validation errors and focus handling
Kept clinical inputs out of URLs and server logs by accepting POST bodies only, with CSRF protection on the prediction endpoint
metrics: 87.8% accuracy, 92.9% recall on the disease class
205-record held-out test set, fixed seeds throughout

localAi.title: Self-hosted LLM with RAG Search
localAi.context: Gia Cat Technology Solutions · internal product · sole developer
localAi.description: A language model running on internal hardware with no GPU, with a retrieval pipeline over the company's own business documents. Piloted by internal ERP teams; not rolled out company-wide yet.
responsibilities: Set up and configured the local LLM server, evaluating hardware and inference constraints on GPU-less infrastructure
Selected a quantized model and tuned its parameters to make CPU-only inference usable
Built a RAG pipeline and document knowledge base behind an internal chatbot, with a lightweight web UI used to test response speed and answer accuracy
Compared cloud and on-premise options for the workload, then chose on-premise given the infrastructure constraints
metrics: ~50 tokens/s on CPU-only hardware, read from the inference server log

erpWarehouse.title: ERP Warehouse & Invoice Integration
erpWarehouse.context: Gia Cat Technology Solutions · client in accounting and warehousing · team of 6
erpWarehouse.description: Fitted the ERP platform to the client's warehouse and accounting processes, and connected it to an external invoice service in both directions — pulling supplier invoices in, and exposing inventory and invoice data back out for another in-house system to read.
responsibilities: Owned the Warehouse module and the accounts payable / receivable document flows
Built a PL/SQL integration with the Bizzi invoice API over UTL_HTTP to pull invoice data automatically
Built ORDS REST endpoints exposing invoice and inventory data to another in-house system on the client side
Logged failed calls to an error table for follow-up

REST endpoints consumed by a second in-house system

about.title: About
paragraphs: I joined Gia Cat Technology Solutions as a back-end intern in 2024 and stayed on as a full stack developer. The work is internal business systems — ERP platforms for construction, manufacturing and accounting teams — where a feature is only finished when the people on the factory floor or in the accounts department can actually use it.

Most of what I do sits between systems. Pulling supplier invoices in from a third-party API, exposing inventory data back out over REST, pushing database changes to a Node.js service in real time. The interesting problems are usually at the seams.

I am also the person on the team who gets asked to evaluate new technology and bring it into the system: push notifications, real-time notifications, the real-time chat platform, and most recently a self-hosted LLM with retrieval search. The first three are in daily use; the last one is in pilot.
